question: What is the main goal of Quality Assurance in nursing?

options.A: To punish staff who make mistakes
options.B: To increase the number of daily admissions
options.C: To reduce the cost of hospital drugs
options.D: To prevent care errors before they happen

explanation: You've got this! Quality assurance is all about staying a step ahead. Instead of waiting for a mistake, we use ongoing checks to keep our patients safe from the get-go. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h1)

question: How does Quality Assurance differ from simple quality control?

options.A: QA focuses entirely on equipment, while control focuses on patients
options.B: QA is proactive and systemic, while control usually catches errors after they occur
options.C: QA is done once a year, while control is done daily
options.D: QA only applies to doctors, while control applies to nurses

explanation: Think of QA as setting up safety nets across the whole system ahead of time, whereas quality control is more like checking things after the job is done to catch any slip-ups. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is a main objective of setting clinical standards in Quality Assurance?

options.A: Ensuring every nurse performs procedures the same safe way
options.B: Making sure doctors do all the documentation
options.C: Eliminating the need for patient handovers
options.D: Reducing the number of nursing shifts per week

explanation: Spot on! Clinical standards act like a reliable compass. They make sure that no matter who is on duty, every patient gets the same safe, top-notch care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h2)

question: A ward manager notices high rates of patient falls. Which QA objective is most relevant to addressing this?
explanation: When we spot hazards like patient falls, our main goal is risk reduction—taking smart steps to protect our patients from getting hurt on the ward. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h2)

question: What does the 'structure' component of the Donabedian model refer to?

options.A: The steps taken to administer an injection
options.B: The final recovery rate of the patient
options.C: The hospital environment, staff, and equipment
options.D: The financial profit of the clinic

explanation: Easy peasy! In the Donabedian model, 'structure' is the foundation—it's about the tools, buildings, and skilled staff we have available to do our work. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why must quality assurance decisions be data-driven rather than based on guesswork?

options.A: Data collection completely eliminates all human error
options.B: Data provides accurate proof of where problems exist and if changes actually work
options.C: Hospital management only accepts reports written in numbers
options.D: Guesswork is illegal for registered nurses in Nigeria

explanation: In nursing, we rely on facts! Real data gives us clear proof of what's going wrong and whether our new ideas are actually fixing the problem. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of a clinical audit in a hospital?

options.A: Comparing current nursing practice against established standards
options.B: Counting the number of visitors on a ward
options.C: Calculating the monthly salary of nursing staff
options.D: Checking the expiration dates of food in the canteen

explanation: A clinical audit is simply checking our actual bedside practice against the golden standard of care to see how well we are doing. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why are anonymous incident reporting systems important for quality assurance?

options.B: They stop patients from seeing hospital records
options.C: They allow nurses to blame doctors for ward mistakes
options.D: They encourage staff to report near-misses and errors without fear of harsh punishment

explanation: When staff don't have to fear being victimized, they speak up about close calls. That honesty helps the whole team fix system flaws before someone gets hurt. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why are bedside nurses considered central to hospital quality assurance?

options.A: They are responsible for hospital budget approvals
options.B: They spend the most time directly caring for patients
options.C: They write all the medical textbooks in the country
options.D: They alone have the power to hire new doctors

explanation: You know it! Because you are right there at the bedside 24/7, you are in the best position to catch safety gaps and make care better. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which task best shows a staff nurse directly participating in quality assurance?

options.A: Reporting a faulty intravenous pump before it harms a patient
options.B: Complaining about low salary during a shift handover
options.C: Refusing to help clean a patient after an accident
options.D: Leaving ward charts blank until the end of the week

explanation: Brilliant! Spotting a broken tool and speaking up before it hurts a patient is the textbook definition of proactive quality assurance in action. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is a common resource barrier faced by nurses trying to maintain quality care in Nigeria?

options.A: An excess of trained nurses with no patients to care for
options.B: Too much free time leading to staff boredom
options.C: Having too many modern computers on every ward
options.D: Shortages of basic consumables like gloves and disinfectants

explanation: It's a tough reality, but lacking basic tools like gloves and clean water makes it super hard to maintain standard infection control. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h6)

question: How does a harsh blame culture negatively affect quality assurance efforts?

options.A: It causes patients to leave the hospital against medical advice
options.B: It drives staff to hide mistakes rather than report them for team learning
options.C: It speeds up the process of patient discharge too much
options.D: It forces the hospital to buy more expensive medical drugs

explanation: When people are afraid of harsh punishments, mistakes get swept under the rug. An open, supportive culture helps us learn and grow instead! [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h6)

question: What does continuous professional development help maintain in a nursing team?

options.A: Fewer working hours for night shifts
options.B: A lower overall patient bed capacity
options.C: Strict separation between doctors and nurses
options.D: Up-to-date clinical knowledge and best practices

explanation: Spot on! Keeping our skills fresh through continuous learning ensures we give our patients the very best, modern care possible. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why is it important for hospital leadership to show staff that audit data leads to real changes?

options.A: It proves that managers do all the heavy work on the ward
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future ward meetings
options.C: It motivates staff to keep participating honestly in quality data collection
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about their treatment

explanation: When nurses see that their reports actually solve real ward problems, they feel valued and stay excited to help make things better. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h7)
